name: opcua-mcp-server
description: Read industrial sensors and control equipment on any OPC UA server.
long_description:
Connects Claude to any OPC UA server — a PLC, a SCADA gateway, a historian or a simulator — and exposes it as MCP tools: read and write nodes, browse the address space, call methods, and read history and server-side aggregates.

Set the endpoint below to your OPC UA server's URL, for example `opc.tcp://192.168.0.10:4840`.

**Security:** the remaining settings are optional and default to an unencrypted, anonymous connection, which is fine for a simulator or a lab server. Against real equipment, set a security policy (Basic256Sha256 unless your server is older) with a client certificate and key, and a username and password. Note that this server can **write nodes and call methods**, so scope the OPC UA account it logs in as to exactly what you intend Claude to be able to do.

opcua_server_url.title: OPC UA endpoint
opcua_server_url.description: URL of the OPC UA server to connect to, e.g. opc.tcp://192.168.0.10:4840

opcua_security_policy.title: Security policy
opcua_security_policy.description: Encryption suite to negotiate: None, Basic128Rsa15, Basic256, Basic256Sha256, Aes128_Sha256_RsaOaep or Aes256_Sha256_RsaPss. Leave blank for an unencrypted connection. Anything other than None needs the certificate and key below.

opcua_security_mode.title: Security mode
opcua_security_mode.description: Sign or SignAndEncrypt. Leave blank to let the policy choose, which means SignAndEncrypt.

opcua_client_cert.title: Client certificate
opcua_client_cert.description: PEM or DER certificate this client presents. Required by any policy other than None.

opcua_client_key.title: Client private key
opcua_client_key.description: Private key matching the certificate above.

opcua_password.title: Password
opcua_password.description: Required if a username is set. Sent in clear text unless a security policy is configured.
